rationale: Initial baseline plan for gemm_128x4096x4096 (M=128,N=4096,K=4096). Domains chosen so tiles divide M/N/K: block_M in {16,32,64,128} divides 128; block_N in {32,64,128,256} divides 4096; block_K in {32,64,128} divides 4096. num_stages 1-4 and threads 64/128/256 included for exploration, but swizzle restricted to [0] to establish a conventional row-major baseline as instructed. Shared limit 32768 (also within the hard portability cap) to keep register/shared pressure conservative for Metal/GB10 portability; estimate = max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) will bind for large tiles at high stages. Equal weights 1 for traffic, launches, pipeline, footprint to get an unbiased first ranking. Note M has a single tile row for block_M=128, so swizzle reuse gains are moot there; larger N tiles reduce launches but increase footprint, and smaller block_M may add parallelism. Next hypothesis after baseline: perturb thread domain (e.g., 256) and block_K (e.g., 128) to test register/pipeline trade-offs, then expand swizzle to [0,4,8,16,32,64] once row-major baseline is measured.
